bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in librpc where ndr_pull_charset_to_null() does not properly check string lengths.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved run feeds the staged 68-byte witness to Samba's `fuzz_ndr_spoolss_TYPE_STRUCT`. The first four bytes are the generic NDR fuzz header `00 00 03 00`, so the harness keeps `type = TYPE_STRUCT`, selects public struct 3, and passes the remaining 64 bytes as stub data into `ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode`. In that parser, the first field is `[charset(UTF16),to_null] uint16 devicename[32]`, so `ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode` calls `ndr_pull_charset_to_null(..., size_devicename_0, sizeof(uint16_t), CH_UTF16)` with a declared length of 32 UTF-16 elements. `ndr_pull_charset_to_null` checks only that `length * byte_mul` bytes are present, then calls `ndr_string_length` without passing the 32-element bound. The staged 64-byte payload contains no `0x0000` UTF-16 element, so `ndr_string_length` keeps probing until the 33rd comparison reads 2 bytes at the first address past the 68-byte heap allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow read in `ndr_string_length` with stack `ndr_string_length -> ndr_pull_charset_to_null -> ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode`. The staged patch resolves this by replacing the unbounded scan with the length-bounded helper `ndr_string_n_length(..., length, byte_mul)`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled stub bytes as the fixed UTF-16 `spoolss_DeviceMode.devicename` field and passes its declared field length into the vulnerable helper.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_19385/poc` has sha256 `10a68f467dfe49c088efdd30c74187da7cc0cd1b7b9547bad19b0a7d191ea3f1`. It is exactly 68 bytes: a 4-byte NDR fuzz header `00 00 03 00` followed by 64 bytes of stub data. After the harness strips the header, those 64 bytes become the first `spoolss_DeviceMode` field consumed here, and their 32 UTF-16 words contain no `0x0000` terminator.

tainted_value_origin.code:
DATA_BLOB blob = data_blob_const(data + HEADER_SIZE,
                         size - HEADER_SIZE);
tainted_value_origin.description: The harness materializes the attacker-controlled parser blob by discarding the 4-byte fuzz header and exposing the remaining 64 bytes as the NDR stub later parsed as `spoolss_DeviceMode`.

root_cause.description: After checking only the raw field byte count, the helper calls `ndr_string_length` without the declared 32-element bound. The later `MIN(str_len, length)` clamp is sequenced after this scan and cannot prevent the overread.
root_cause.note: The fix in `patch.diff` replaces this call with `ndr_string_n_length(ndr->data+ndr->offset, length, byte_mul)`, which preserves the declared field bound during the terminator search.

sink.description: ASan sink. The unbounded UTF-16 terminator probe reaches the 33rd element and issues a 2-byte `memcmp` read one word past the 64-byte `devicename` field.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 2` at the first byte past the 68-byte witness allocation. Because the harness stripped a 4-byte header before the project parser ran, that address is exactly `blob_start + 64`, i.e. one UTF-16 element past the 64-byte field scanned here.

parser_admitted.description: After the 4-byte header is accepted and dispatched to the TYPE_STRUCT parser, the harness enters the project puller with `f->ndr_pull(ndr_pull, pull_push_print_flags, st);`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness accepts the 4-byte NDR fuzz header, selects the TYPE_STRUCT parser path for struct id 3, strips the header, and exposes the remaining 64 bytes as the stub blob.
The generated `spoolss_DeviceMode` parser consumes that stub as the first fixed UTF-16 field `devicename[32]` and hands it to `ndr_pull_charset_to_null`.
The helper skips its empty-string early return, checks only that 64 raw bytes are present, and then invokes `ndr_string_length` without the declared 32-element bound.
Because the 64-byte field contains no UTF-16 zero word, the terminator scan keeps calling `memcmp` until the 33rd probe reads 2 bytes past the end of the heap-backed witness.

fine_trace.code:
DATA_BLOB blob = data_blob_const(data + HEADER_SIZE,
                         size - HEADER_SIZE);
fine_trace.note: The target keeps the generic 4-byte NDR fuzz header. In the staged witness, bytes 0..1 are `0x0000`, so `type = TYPE_STRUCT`, bytes 2..3 are `0x0003`, and the remaining 64 bytes become the stub blob passed into the NDR puller. The saved stack shows this header selects `ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode`.

Source. The generated parser consumes the blob's first field as `[charset(UTF16),to_null] devicename[MAXDEVICENAME]`. The immediately preceding line sets `size_devicename_0 = MAXDEVICENAME`; local `spoolss.idl` defines `MAXDEVICENAME = 32`, so this call hands the helper a 32-element UTF-16 field with `byte_mul = 2` backed by exactly the 64 payload bytes from step 1.

The helper's only early exit for empty strings is skipped. Here `length` is the fixed field length 32 from step 2, so execution continues into the non-empty path that scans the buffer for a terminator.
This computes the raw field extent as `32 * 2 = 64` bytes and verifies only that those 64 bytes are present at the current offset. It does not require a UTF-16 zero element within that extent.

Root cause. The code drops the declared field bound and calls the terminator scanner with only the data pointer and element size. The later `str_len = MIN(str_len, length)` on line 633 would run only after this helper returns, so it cannot protect the scan itself.

Sink. The 64-byte `devicename` payload holds 32 UTF-16 words and none of them is `0x0000`, so the loop stays true through all 32 in-bounds elements. At `i == 32`, the next `memcmp` reads 2 bytes at `var + 64`, which is exactly the first address past the 68-byte witness allocation reported by ASan (4-byte header plus the 64-byte field).

sanitizer_ground_truth.dedup_token: MemcmpInterceptorCommon(void*, int (*)(void const*, void const*, unsigned long), void const*, void const*, unsigned long)--bcmp--ndr_string_length
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from the staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json, then cross-checked against the exact generated build-tree sources still present in the live Stage 01 workspace container

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan allocates one 68-byte heap buffer for the entire witness. Step 1 strips the 4-byte fuzz header, leaving exactly 64 bytes of stub data, and step 2 consumes that entire stub as `devicename[32]`. Step 6's `var + 64` probe therefore lands exactly at the first byte past the same 68-byte allocation ASan reports.

evidence_note: The exact generated files `bin/default/librpc/gen_ndr/ndr_spoolss.c` and `bin/default/lib/fuzzing/fuzz_ndr_spoolss_TYPE_STRUCT.c` were read directly from the already-running Stage 01 workspace container `gt-arvo_19385-workspace`, because only the checked-in source tree is mirrored under `_work/src` on the host. Those emitted lines match the saved ASan stack, the local `spoolss.idl`, and the local PIDL template in `Parser.pm`.
patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged patch changes `ndr_pull_charset_to_null` to use `ndr_string_n_length(ndr->data+ndr->offset, length, byte_mul)`, which preserves the declared field length while searching for a terminator and prevents the step-6 out-of-bounds probe.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 saved `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_19385 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which ran `/out/fuzz_ndr_spoolss_TYPE_STRUCT /tmp/poc` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` with stack `ndr_string_length -> ndr_pull_charset_to_null -> ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode`.

format.name: Samba NDR TYPE_STRUCT fuzz input
format.contract: Exactly the staged 68-byte blob `gt_results/arvo_19385/poc` with sha256 `10a68f467dfe49c088efdd30c74187da7cc0cd1b7b9547bad19b0a7d191ea3f1`. Bytes 0..1 are fuzz flags `0x0000`, so the target stays on `TYPE_STRUCT`; bytes 2..3 are struct selector `0x0003`; bytes 4..67 are the 64-byte NDR stub. On the observed path, that header dispatches the stub to `ndr_pull_spoolss_DeviceMode`, whose first field is the fixed `[charset(UTF16),to_null] devicename[32]`. Those 64 stub bytes contain no `0x0000` UTF-16 word, so the vulnerable build searches past the declared 32-element field and `ndr_string_length` performs the reported 2-byte overread. The saved artifacts do not justify any broader claim about other struct selectors or other UTF-16 payload classes.
